novelty_flags.label: Related work and Theorem 1 / Theorem 2 survey
novelty_flags.one_line: Add Kumar and Sinha, “Disentangling Mixtures of Unknown Causal Interventions” (UAI 2021): it proves component/target identification from a pooled mixture of perfect interventions given a known discrete CBN, so it does not subsume this Gaussian hidden-baseline result but is a closer omitted comparator.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 14–15, Appendix F.2 Proposition 10 and Appendix G
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Proposition 10 states that an observational context is the argmin of the deviation-rank score; Appendix G says rank-at-most-two is necessary but not sufficient and leaves a model-membership test to future work.

Theorem 4.1 treats a fixed number of soft-atomic-intervention components and recovers mixture parameters under effective intervention and faithfulness; Corollary 4.1.1 additionally assumes samples from the observational distribution and I-faithfulness for I-MEC recovery.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 6, Assumption 1 and Theorem 1; p. 7, Theorem 3
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper estimates intervention targets from precision differences for observational/interventional datasets, assumes I-faithfulness for consistency, and gives finite-sample target/parent recovery guarantees.
The paper characterizes an interventional Markov equivalence class under unknown targets and gives a provably consistent algorithm from observational and interventional data.
The paper characterizes the equivalence class of Gaussian SCMs under unknown interventions and derives the GnIES greedy recovery procedure.
Theorem 1.1 clusters centered nonspherical Gaussian mixtures with dimension-polynomial cost under pairwise total-variation separation of the form 1-f(w_min), i.e. near-disjoint components.
The paper gives operator-norm concentration and moment bounds for sample covariance operators from iid centered Gaussian observations in terms of effective rank.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 1, abstract; pp. 2–5, setup and contribution summary
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper obtains constructive perfect-intervention recovery using nonzero higher-order cumulants, hence non-Gaussianity, in a latent linear causal-disentanglement setting.

The paper studies pooled mixtures of perfect interventions on a given finite discrete CBN and proves unique recovery of intervention tuples under positivity and an exclusion condition; it assumes access to the baseline CBN and is therefore not a subsuming comparator.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Kumar and Sinha (UAI 2021) to related work and state precisely that its known-baseline discrete-CBN premise is what the coordinate certificate removes in the centered Gaussian fully-covered subclass.

Make the membership theorem’s novelty contrast explicit: state as a corollary that the certificate decides exact compatibility of an arbitrary unordered tuple, whereas Squires et al.’s Appendix G rank screen is only necessary.

For the statistical OEQ, use Anderson et al.’s exact separation condition TV at least 1-f(w_min) as the benchmark and formulate a concrete surgery-geometry condition that is provably weaker or prove that no such weakening is possible.

recommended_next_step: Revise the literature map and theorem gaps to include the omitted UAI 2021 comparator, then advance this field-tier exact-identification angle to Stage 0.
